html:
Twyfelfontein is a valley in the Kunene region of northwest Namibia with over two thousand rock engravings of animals, footprints and signs, made by hunter-gatherers over many centuries; it was listed by UNESCO in 2007.

The carvings show giraffe, rhino, elephant, ostrich and a famous lion with a long tail and paw prints. They were made by the ancestors of the San, probably for rituals of healers who believed they entered the spirit world. Later Khoekhoe herders added some paintings and engravings.

The site shows the long history of people in the desert of Namibia, long before Herero herders and German settlers arrived. It is now one of Namibia's main sites for visitors, close to the San heritage of the region.
